plan: 1 Kings 22:10-28; 2 Chronicles 18:9-27; 1 Kings 22:29-35; 2 Chronicles 18:28-34; 1 Kings 22:36-40, 51-53; 2 Chronicles 19:1-11; 2 Chronicles 20:1-30

readings.title: The Council of the False Prophets
readings.subtitle: The sovereigns seek counsel, but a spirit of harmony with falsehood prevails.
readings.text: [1 Kings 22:10] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl and Yehoshaphat sovereign of Yehuḏah were sitting, each on his throne, dressed in their robes, at a threshing-floor at the entrance of the gate of Shomeron. And all the prophets were prophesying before them. [11] And Tsiḏqiyah son of Kena‛anah had made horns of iron for himself, and said, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘With these you push <dn>את</dn> the Arameans until they are destroyed.’ ” [12] And all the prophets were prophesying so, saying, “Go up to Ramoth Gil‛aḏ and prosper, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall give it into the hand of the sovereign.” [13] And the messenger who had gone to call Miḵayehu spoke to him, saying, “See now, the words of the prophets with one mouth are good towards the sovereign. Please, let your word be like the word of one of them, and you shall speak good.” [14] And Miḵayehu said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, whatever <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> says to me, that <dn>I</dn> speak.”

readings.title: The Verdict of the Heavenly Court
readings.subtitle: Miḵayehu reveals YeHoVaH’s authorized deception to execute justice upon Aḥaḇ.
readings.text: [15] And he came to the sovereign, and the sovereign said to him, “Miḵayehu, do we go against Ramoth Gil‛aḏ to battle, or do we refrain?” And he answered him, “Go and prosper, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall give it into the hand of the sovereign!” [16] And the sovereign said to him, “How many times have <dn>I</dn> made you swear that you do not speak to me, except the truth, in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?” [17] So he said, “<dn>I</dn> saw all Yisra’ěl scattered on the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, ‘These have no master. Let everyone return to his house in peace.’ ” [18] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl said to Yehoshaphat, “Have <dn>I</dn> not said to you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?” [19] Then he said, “Therefore hear the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: <dn>I</dn> saw <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sitting on <dn>His</dn> throne, and all the host of the heavens standing by <dn>Him</dn>, on <dn>His</dn> right and on <dn>His</dn> left. [20] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, ‘Who shall entice <dn>את</dn> Aḥaḇ to go up and fall at Ramoth Gil‛aḏ?’ And this one said this, and another said that. [21] “And a spirit came forward and stood before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, ‘Let me entice him.’ [22] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, ‘In what way?’ And he said, ‘<dn>I</dn> shall go out and be a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all his prophets.’ And <dn>He</dn> said, ‘Entice him, and also prevail. Go out and do so.’ [23] “And now, see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has put a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken evil concerning you.”

readings.title: The Imprisonment of the True Prophet
readings.subtitle: The physical consequence of speaking the absolute truth of YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [24] And Tsiḏqiyahu son of Kena‛anah came near and struck Miḵayehu on the cheek, and said, “Where did the spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> pass over from me to speak to you?” [25] And Miḵayehu said, “Look, you shall see on that day when you go into an inner room to hide!” [26] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl said, “Take Miḵayehu, and return him to Amon the governor of the city, and to Yo’ash son of the sovereign, [27] and say, ‘Thus said the sovereign, “Put this one in prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and water of affliction until <dn>I</dn> come in peace.” ’ ” [28] And Miḵayehu said, “If you ever return in peace, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not spoken by me.” And he said, “Hear, all you people!”

readings.title: The Assembly of Enticement
readings.subtitle: A parallel witness to the unified voice of the false prophets.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 18:9] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl and Yehoshaphat the sovereign of Yehuḏah, dressed in their robes, sat each on his throne. And they sat at a threshing-floor at the entrance of the gate of Shomeron. And all the prophets were prophesying before them. [10] And Tsiḏqiyahu son of Kena‛anah had made horns of iron for himself, and said, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘With these you push <dn>את</dn> the Arameans until they are destroyed.’ ” [11] And all the prophets were prophesying so, saying, “Go up to Ramoth Gil‛aḏ and prosper, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall give it into the hand of the sovereign.” [12] And the messenger who had gone to call Miḵayehu spoke to him, saying, “See, the words of the prophets with one mouth are good towards the sovereign. So please let your word be like the word of one of them, and you shall speak good.” [13] And Miḵayehu said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, whatever my <dn>Elohim</dn> says, that <dn>I</dn> speak.”

readings.title: The Adversary as an Authorized Tool
readings.subtitle: The spirit of falsehood is deployed by YeHoVaH to extract what is rightfully due.
readings.text: [14] And he came to the sovereign. And the sovereign said to him, “Miḵah, do we go against Ramoth Gil‛aḏ to battle, or do <dn>I</dn> refrain?” And he said, “Go and prosper, and they are given into your hand!” [15] And the sovereign said to him, “How many times have <dn>I</dn> made you swear that you do not speak to me, except the truth, in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?” [16] So he said, “<dn>I</dn> saw all Yisra’ěl scattered on the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, ‘These have no master. Let each return to his house in peace.’ ” [17] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl said to Yehoshaphat, “Did <dn>I</dn> not say to you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?” [18] Then he said, “Therefore hear the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: <dn>I</dn> saw <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sitting on <dn>His</dn> throne, and all the host of the heavens standing on <dn>His</dn> right and on <dn>His</dn> left. [19] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, ‘Who shall entice <dn>את</dn> Aḥaḇ sovereign of Yisra’ěl to go up and fall at Ramoth Gil‛aḏ?’ And one said this, and another said that. [20] “And a spirit came forward and stood before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, ‘Let me entice him.’ <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, ‘In what way?’ [21] “And he said, ‘<dn>I</dn> shall go out and be a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all his prophets.’ And <dn>He</dn> said, ‘Entice him, and also prevail. Go out and do so.’ [22] “And now, see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has put a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of these prophets of yours, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken evil concerning you.”

readings.title: Bread and Water of Affliction
readings.subtitle: Miḵayehu anchors his trust in the structural guarantee of YeHoVaH’s word.
readings.text: [23] And Tsiḏqiyahu son of Kena‛anah came near and struck Miḵayehu on the cheek, and said, “Which way did the spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> pass over from me to speak to you?” [24] And Miḵayehu said, “Look, you shall see on that day when you go into an inner room to hide!” [25] Then the sovereign of Yisra’ěl said, “Take Miḵayehu, and return him to Amon the governor of the city and to Yo’ash the sovereign’s son, [26] and say, ‘Thus said the sovereign, “Put this one in prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and water of affliction until <dn>I</dn> return in peace.” ’ ” [27] And Miḵayehu said, “If you return at all in peace, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not spoken by me.” And he said, “Hear, all you people!”

readings.title: The Futility of Disguise
readings.subtitle: No human strategy can evade the precise extraction of divine justice.
readings.text: [1 Kings 22:29] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl and Yehoshaphat the sovereign of Yehuḏah went up to Ramoth Gil‛aḏ. [30] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl said to Yehoshaphat, “Let me disguise myself and go into battle, but you put on your robes.” So the sovereign of Yisra’ěl disguised himself and went into battle. [31] And the sovereign of Aram had commanded the thirty-two commanders of his chariots, saying, “Fight with no one small or great, but only with the sovereign of Yisra’ěl.” [32] And it came to be, when the commanders of the chariots saw Yehoshaphat, that they said, “Indeed, it is the sovereign of Yisra’ěl!” So they turned aside to fight against him, and Yehoshaphat cried out. [33] And it came to be, when the commanders of the chariots saw that it was not the sovereign of Yisra’ěl, that they turned back from pursuing him. [34] And a man drew a bow in his simplicity, and struck the sovereign of Yisra’ěl between the joints of his armour. And he said to the driver of his chariot, “Turn around and take me out of the battle, for <dn>I</dn> am wounded.” [35] And the battle increased that day. And the sovereign was propped up in his chariot, facing the Arameans, and died at evening, and the blood ran out from the wound onto the floor of the chariot.

readings.title: The Unerring Arrow
readings.subtitle: Yehoshaphat cries out for the Lifted Face of YeHoVaH while Aḥaḇ meets his decreed end.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 18:28] Then the sovereign of Yisra’ěl and Yehoshaphat the sovereign of Yehuḏah went up to Ramoth Gil‛aḏ. [29] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl said to Yehoshaphat, “Let me disguise myself and go into battle, but you put on your robes.” And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl disguised himself, and they went into battle. [30] And the sovereign of Aram had commanded the commanders of the chariots who were with him, saying, “Fight with no one small or great, but only with the sovereign of Yisra’ěl.” [31] And it came to be, when the commanders of the chariots saw Yehoshaphat, that they said, “It is the sovereign of Yisra’ěl!” So they turned around to fight against him, and Yehoshaphat cried out, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> helped him, and <dn>Elohim</dn> moved them to turn away from him. [32] And it came to be, when the commanders of the chariots saw that it was not the sovereign of Yisra’ěl, that they turned back from pursuing him. [33] And a man drew a bow in his simplicity, and struck the sovereign of Yisra’ěl between the joints of his armour. And he said to the driver of his chariot, “Turn around and take me out of the battle, for <dn>I</dn> am wounded.” [34] But the battle increased that day, and the sovereign of Yisra’ěl was propped up in his chariot facing the Arameans until evening, and he died at the time of the going down of the sun.

readings.title: The Prophecy Vindicated
readings.subtitle: The exact fulfillment of YeHoVaH’s spoken consequence upon the house of Aḥaḇ.
readings.text: [1 Kings 22:36] And as the sun was going down, a shout passed through the camp, saying, “Each to his city, and each to his land!” [37] So the sovereign died and was brought to Shomeron, and they buried the sovereign in Shomeron. [38] And when the chariot was washed at a pool in Shomeron, the dogs licked up his blood, where the whores bathed, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> had spoken. [39] And the rest of the acts of Aḥaḇ and all that he did, and the ivory house which he built and all the cities that he built, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl? [40] So Aḥaḇ slept with his fathers, and Aḥazyahu his son reigned in his place.

readings.title: The Continuation of Rebellion
readings.subtitle: Aḥazyahu perpetuates the systemic corruption of his father and mother.
readings.text: [1 Kings 22:51] Aḥazyahu son of Aḥaḇ began to reign over Yisra’ěl in Shomeron in the seventeenth year of Yehoshaphat sovereign of Yehuḏah, and reigned two years over Yisra’ěl, [52] and did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and walked in the way of his father and in the way of his mother and in the way of Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ěl sin, [53] and served Ba‛al and bowed himself to it, and provoked <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, according to all that his father had done.

readings.title: The Seer's Rebuke
readings.subtitle: Yehoshaphat is confronted for aligning with those who hate the harmony of YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 19:1] And Yehoshaphat the sovereign of Yehuḏah returned to his house in peace in Yerushalayim. [2] And Yěhu son of Ḥanani the seer went out to face him, and said to Sovereign Yehoshaphat, “Do you help the wrong and love those who hate <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? Therefore the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is upon you. [3] “But good matters are found in you, in that you have removed the Ashěroth from the land, and have prepared your heart to seek <dn>Elohim</dn>.”

readings.title: The Architecture of Right-Ruling
readings.subtitle: Establishing a civil system based on the strict justice and impartiality of YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [4] So Yehoshaphat dwelt in Yerushalayim, and he went out again among the people from Be’ěrsheḇa to the hill country of Ephrayim, and brought them back to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers. [5] And he appointed judges in the land in all the walled cities of Yehuḏah, city by city, [6] and said to the judges, “Watch what you are doing, for you do not judge for man, but for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who is with you in the matter of right-ruling. [7] “And now, let the fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be upon you. Guard and do it, for there is no unrighteousness with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, nor partiality, nor taking of bribes.” [8] And in Yerushalayim Yehoshaphat also appointed some of the Lěvites and priests, and some of the chief fathers of Yisra’ěl, for the right-ruling of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and for dispute. Then they returned to Yerushalayim. [9] And he commanded them, saying, “Do this in the fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, trustworthily and with a perfect heart: [10] “When any dispute comes to you from your brothers who dwell in their cities, between blood and blood, between Torah and command, laws and right-rulings, then you shall warn them, lest they trespass against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and wrath come upon you and your brothers. Do this, and you shall not be guilty. [11] “And look, Amaryahu the chief priest is over you in all matters of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And Zeḇaḏyahu son of Yishma‛ěl, the ruler of the house of Yehuḏah, for all the matters of the sovereign, and the Lěvites are officials before you. Be strong and do, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with the good.”

readings.title: A Multitude from Beyond the Sea
readings.subtitle: Facing annihilation, Yehoshaphat unifies the nation to seek the protection of YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 20:1] And after this it came to be that the children of Mo’aḇ and the children of Ammon came in, and with them some of the peoples, against Yehoshaphat to battle. [2] And they came and spoke to Yehoshaphat, saying, “A great army is coming against you from beyond the sea, from Aram. And see, they are in Ḥatsatson Tamar,” which is Ěn Geḏi. [3] And Yehoshaphat was afraid, and set his face to seek <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Yehuḏah. [4] And Yehuḏah gathered to inquire of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, even from all the cities of Yehuḏah they came to seek <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: Pleading the Covenant
readings.subtitle: Yehuḏah relies on the historic guarantee of the House and the absolute authority of their Elohim.
readings.text: [5] And Yehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim, in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in front of the new courtyard, [6] and said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of our fathers, are <dn>You</dn> not <dn>Elohim</dn> in the heavens, and do <dn>You</dn> not rule over all the reigns of the nations, and in <dn>Your</dn> hand is there not power and might, so that no one is able to stand against <dn>You</dn>? [7] “Are <dn>You</dn> not our <dn>Elohim</dn>? <dn>You</dn> have driven out <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of this land before <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ěl, and gave it to the seed of Aḇraham who loves <dn>You</dn> forever. [8] “And they dwell in it, and have built <dn>You</dn> a set-apart place in it for <dn>Your</dn> Name, saying, [9] If evil does come upon us, such as the sword, judgment, or pestilence, or scarcity of food, we shall stand before this House and in <dn>Your</dn> presence – for <dn>Your</dn> Name is in this House – and cry out to <dn>You</dn> in our distress, and <dn>You</dn> do hear and save.’ [10] “And now, see, the children of Ammon and Mo’aḇ, and Mount Sě‛ir, whom <dn>You</dn> would not let Yisra’ěl invade when they came out of the land of Mitsrayim, for they turned from them and did not destroy them, [11] and see, they are repaying us by coming in to drive us out of <dn>Your</dn> possession which <dn>You</dn> have given us to inherit. [12] “O our <dn>Elohim</dn>, would <dn>You</dn> not judge them? For we are powerless against this great army that is coming against us. And we do not know what to do, but our eyes are upon <dn>You</dn>.” [13] And all Yehuḏah, with their little ones, their wives, and their children, stood before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Battle Belongs to YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: The Spirit commands them to stand still and witness the physical execution of salvation.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 20:14] And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came upon Yaḥazi’ěl son of Zeḵaryahu, son of Benayah, son of Ye‛i’ěl, son of Mattanyah, a Lěvite of the sons of Asaph, in the midst of the assembly, [15] and he said, “Listen, all Yehuḏah, and you inhabitants of Yerushalayim, and Sovereign Yehoshaphat! Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to you, <dq>‘Do not fear, nor be afraid of the face of this great army, for the battle is not yours, but <dn>Elohim</dn>’s.</dq> [16] <dq>Go down against them tomorrow. See, they are coming up by the ascent of Tsits, and you shall find them at the end of the wadi before the Wilderness of Yeru’ěl.</dq> [17] <dq>It is not for you to fight in this. Position yourselves, stand still and see the deliverance of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with you, O Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim!’ Do not be afraid nor fear, go out against them tomorrow, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with you.</dq>”

readings.title: Trust Preceding the Victory
readings.subtitle: The assembly enacts functional trust by praising YeHoVaH before the conflict begins.
readings.text: [18] And Yehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground, and all Yehuḏah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim fell down before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to bow themselves before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [19] And the Lěvites, of the children of the Qehathites and of the children of the Qorḥites stood up to praise <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl with exceedingly loud voice. [20] And they rose early in the morning and went out into the Wilderness of Teqova. And as they went out, Yehoshaphat stood and said, “Hear me, O Yehuḏah and you inhabitants of Yerushalayim: Trust in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> and be steadfast, trust <dn>His</dn> prophets and prosper.” [21] And after consulting with the people, he appointed those who should sing to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and who should praise the splendour of set-apartness, as they went out before the army and were saying, “Give thanks to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>His</dn> loving-commitment is everlasting.”

readings.title: The Adversaries Annihilate Themselves
readings.subtitle: Praise acts as a trigger for YeHoVaH to turn the destructive friction of the enemy inward.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 20:22] And when they began singing and praising, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> set ambushes against the children of Ammon, Mo’aḇ, and Mount Sě‛ir, who had come against Yehuḏah, and they were smitten. [23] Then the children of Ammon and Mo’aḇ stood up against the inhabitants of Mount Sě‛ir to destroy and annihilate them. And when they had made an end of the inhabitants of Sě‛ir, they helped to destroy one another. [24] And when Yehuḏah came at the lookout in the wilderness, they looked toward the army and saw their dead bodies, lying on the ground, and none had escaped.

readings.title: The Valley of Beraḵah
readings.subtitle: Yehuḏah reaps the surplus generated by YeHoVaH’s intervention, securing a season of ultimate rest.
readings.text: [25] And Yehoshaphat and his people came to take away their spoil, and they found among them a great amount of valuables on the dead bodies, and precious jewelry, which they stripped off for themselves, more than they could take away. And they were three days plundering the spoil, for it was much. [26] And on the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beraḵah, for there they blessed <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Therefore the name of that place was called The Valley of Beraḵah to this day. [27] Then they returned, every man of Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim, with Yehoshaphat in front of them, to go back to Yerushalayim with joy, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had made them rejoice over their enemies. [28] And they came to Yerushalayim, with harps and lyres and trumpets, to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [29] And the fear of <dn>Elohim</dn> was on all the reigns of the lands when they heard that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had fought against the enemies of Yisra’ěl. [30] Then the reign of Yehoshaphat was at peace, for his <dn>Elohim</dn> gave him rest on all sides.
